claim: Kalshi (a CFTC-registered exchange) is working with index provider Compute Desk to launch GPU compute futures - GPU rental contracts plus perpetual futures - with no confirmed launch date or final specs and products still subject to regulatory requirements; Kalshi had delisted its compute-power prediction market in August 2026

First OTC option on GPU prices: Architect (through its CFTC-registered introducing-broker affiliate) and Luxor (as swap counterparty) executed a one-year put for Hyperbolic hedging ~$5M of future Nvidia B200 rental revenue, settled monthly against Silicon Data's B200 Rental Price Index (2026-11-17)

Akash (Overclock Labs) unveiled Akash Forwards, a commodity-style forward market for physical-delivery GPU hours (8x B300, H200, RTX Pro 6000) with price fixed at purchase; certified-participant pilot Q1 2027, public launch Q2 2027 - the first on-chain GPU-hour forward order book

Compute Desk (the Compute Index, Inc.) raised a $45M seed led by Lightspeed Venture Partners, with Menlo Ventures, Hedosophia, Motive Partners, Crucible, Inovia, Soma, Mythos, Blue Wire, Firesteak and Drysdale participating, to build compute pricing and clearing (Compute Signal data, Compute Trader liquidity, Compute Clear physical settlement)
ETF issuers are racing to create funds that track compute-futures contracts on AI costs, positioning for launch ahead of regulatory approval while exchanges await CFTC sign-off

H100 index divergence re-widened: Silicon Data SDH100RT $3.10/GPU-hr vs Ornn OCPI-H100 $2.91 on 2026-11-22 - about 6.5% apart, reversing the ~1.3% convergence of 2026-11-15 (Ornn H100 -4.9% on the week, -7.6% over 30 days)
source: Silicon Data H100 index (primary, 2026-11-22) + Ornn OCPI (primary, 2026-11-22)

claim: B200 softened across benchmarks: Ornn OCPI-B200 $9.08/GPU-hr (2026-11-22; -6.0% 7-day, -5.3% 30-day), Silicon Data B200 $6.94; Compute Desk 1-year-reserved readings were B300 $7.21, B200 $6.06, H200 $3.52, H100 $2.90 (2026-11-18)

Derivatives no-change: CFTC product record 62544 (NYMEX Silicon Data H100 Rental Index Futures) remains 'Approval Pending (90)', with the review extended to 2027-01-08 and conditioned on no other registrant self-certifying, obtaining approval, or listing comparable contracts; ICE x Ornn (index data live since 2026-10-05), Nodal x Compute Desk and Architect's US venue remain unlaunched
source: CFTC product record 62544 (primary) + ICE exchange notice (2026-09-29)

claim: Capital/credit layer: Marble launched with an $11M seed led by Polychain (2026-11-10) for compute private credit and OTC forwards; USD.AI led a $106M senior secured facility for NexGen Cloud (216 HGX B300 servers, 1,728 GPUs, Finland; 2026-11-03) through its GPU Loan Exchange; Blue Owl (Citi summit, 2026-11-10) noted neocloud unsecured bonds widened 400-500bps while GPU-financing pricing moved only 50-75bps
source: ABF Journal + PR Newswire + USD.AI blog (2026-11)

claim: NYMEX (CME Group) voluntarily consented to a further 60-day CFTC review extension for its Silicon Data H100 (GPU1) and B200 (GPU2) compute futures, moving the decision date to 2027-01-08; the extension is conditioned on no other CFTC registrant self-certifying, obtaining approval, or listing a comparable contract (an earlier date would control)

CFTC delayed approval of GPU rental futures, citing liquidity and manipulation risk from opaque, concentrated pricing indexes; plans further meetings with benchmark providers, pushing a first compute-futures market to early 2027; DRW, Jump Trading and a16z are pressing for approval

Ornn is in the midst of a triple-tranche funding round at a top valuation of ~$1B, with Thrive Capital and General Catalyst in talks to participate; follows its $33M seed led by a16z crypto in June 2026

Anthropic says it will not terminate its ~$41.3B compute agreement with Lambda despite Lambda missing a deadline to secure a Texas data-center lease; Lambda is pursuing up to $4B in private financing ahead of a possible 2027 IPO
RunPod partners with RUTILEA to expand AI compute capacity in Asia; RUTILEA becomes RunPod's exclusive Japan partner for sourcing and onboarding data-center capacity onto the RunPod platform

Hyperbolic's $30M Series A1 detailed (2026-11-06): aggregating 300+ GPU cloud providers via its Forge control plane, with a planned Global Compute Grid adding spot instances, dynamic pricing, market-making and compute-price hedging

SF Compute operates a physically-settled forwards market that has cleared several hundred million dollars of volume and is positioning the GPU hour as loan collateral, acting as an independent servicer that operates but does not own the clusters it sells
CFTC compute-derivatives RFC (docket CFTC-2026-1850) remains closed since 2026-10-20; published comments ~108; no Commission decision or follow-on action announced

Kalshi operates CFTC-regulated event contracts on GPU rental prices (since March 2026) and published the first market-implied GPU compute forward curve on 2026-07-14 for Nvidia B200, H200 and A100, referencing Ornn's live-trade index

Nvidia signed non-binding MOUs (2026-08-10) with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR to mobilize $500B+ in AI data-center financing with Nvidia GPUs as loan collateral, Nvidia guaranteeing up to 25% of any resale-value decline
Silicon Data raised a $30.5M Series A in August 2026 from Valor Equity Partners and Atreides Management's joint AI fund; it is the index provider for the pending CME/NYMEX H100 and B200 contracts

Architect Financial Technologies acquired a US Designated Contract Market (IMX Health) to launch the American Innovation Exchange, a CFTC-regulated venue for compute and AI-supply-chain futures/options; its compute products (H100/H200/B200/B300, Compute Desk indexes) remain pending approval while FX and metals trade live on Bitnomial's DCM

CME/NYMEX filed two compute futures (Silicon Data H100 GPU1, B200 GPU2) with the CFTC on 2026-08-11 (Submission 26-370): 730 GPU-hours per contract, $7.30/tick, 36-month listing cycle, cash-settled; self-certified under CEA 5c(c)/Reg 40.3(a)
